consequences: Protocol, governed-domain, and governance semantic changes remain independently visible while one full composition and one accepted-temporal epoch stay exact.
A standalone structural graph can evolve its governed-graph role and snapshot without acquiring protocol-ledger or full-composition semantics.
constraints: A full v0 composition has exactly one ProtocolRecordContract, one GovernedGraphContract, and one GovernanceContract, with no fourth or optional role.
Each role-bound identity uses the fixed v0 constructor, exact fixed role tag, and one complete EffectiveContract identity; no role borrows ambient semantics.
The closed composition identity uses its distinct fixed v0 constructor and exactly the three role-bound identities.
Any accepted-temporal semantic role change requires a newly bound composition and a new ledger epoch; independent heads and recovery machinery are deferred.
Logical identity inputs do not select public identifiers, artifact or bundle bytes, persisted wire, governance topology, admission content, migration, package, or API.
data.selected_option: Three exact semantic roles in one closed composition and one v0 accepted-temporal epoch

summary: Accept three exact roles in one closed contract composition.
why: The closed three-role model preserves semantic modularity and queryable change boundaries without creating independent heads, multiple runtimes, or premature wire machinery. One exact composition remains the KISS epoch boundary for accepted-temporal protocol state.
